evals.prompt: I just re-exported my data. ~/Downloads/synology.json is my Plex server export (each movie is a disc I own), the most recent letterboxd-jluszcz export folder in Downloads is my Letterboxd export, and ~/Documents/MovieList/movielist.json has my year-by-year stack-ranked movie lists. Ignoring TV, build me a taste profile, check whether my ranked lists line up with my Letterboxd stars, and recommend discs to buy (I'll blind buy). Write the reports to <OUTPUT_DIR>.
evals.expected_output: movie-taste-profile.md and movie-recommendations.md in the output dir: profile with rating distribution + Spearman-by-year consistency table + tier averages; tiered recommendations including blind buys; chat summary leads with the consistency verdict
assertions: Produces both a taste-profile markdown file and a recommendations markdown file in the outputs directory

Consistency analysis reports per-year rank-vs-rating (Spearman) correlation and characterizes recent years (2022 onward) as strongly consistent — high positive correlation (~0.9 against the 2026-07-07 export; exact values are snapshot-dependent and will drift as data is re-exported)
Does not recommend purchasing movies already in the Plex library (e.g. Knives Out, Top Gun: Maverick, Parasite, and E.T. which is owned under the abbreviated title 'E.T.')
Recommendations include a blind-buy section: unseen films with a stated rationale tied to the user's demonstrated taste
TV shows are excluded from the analysis
Pre-2021 list years are flagged as having sparse rating coverage rather than presented as evidence of inconsistency

evals.prompt: quick question - do the rankings in my movie list (~/Documents/MovieList/movielist.json) actually match the star ratings i give on letterboxd? my letterboxd export is the letterboxd-jluszcz folder in ~/Downloads. curious which movies i'm most inconsistent about. put whatever you produce in <OUTPUT_DIR>
evals.expected_output: Consistency analysis: high Spearman (~0.9) for 2022-2026, sparse-year caveat for pre-2021, and a list of genuine mismatches (e.g. The Nice Guys ranked low/rated 4.5, Flow ranked high/rated 2.5). Should not fabricate ownership recommendations; synology.json not required
assertions: Answers with a clear verdict: rankings and star ratings agree strongly, with recent-year correlation around 0.9
Names specific genuine mismatch films with rank-vs-rating evidence (e.g. The Nice Guys ranked low but rated 4.5, Flow ranked high but rated 2.5, The World's End)
Does not present title-collision false positives as mismatches (e.g. Road House 2024 vs 1989 rating, Suicide Squad 2016 vs The Suicide Squad 2021)
Notes that low correlations in older years reflect sparse rating coverage / later re-rating, not genuine inconsistency
Saves its analysis output to the outputs directory
